evaluations.evidence: view a list of sponsors
evaluations.rationale: Can be implemented as a standalone listing feature without requiring another specific story to be completed first.

evaluations.evidence: view a list of user profiles
evaluations.rationale: Viewing profiles inherently depends on user accounts/profiles existing (registration/profile creation).

evaluations.evidence: email all the trainers at once from the website
evaluations.rationale: Bulk-email capability can be implemented independently; it does not inherently require another backlog story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are
evaluations.rationale: A map page/content can be delivered standalone without depending on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: edit my training node myself
evaluations.rationale: Editing a training node presupposes that training nodes exist and are created/managed elsewhere in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: limit to one registration per day per authenticated user
evaluations.rationale: This constraint depends on having a registration workflow and authenticated users.

evaluations.evidence: admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee
evaluations.rationale: Tracking registration status depends on an attendee registration process and stored registrations.

evaluations.evidence: be added to a training waitlist
evaluations.rationale: Waitlisting inherently depends on an existing training registration/capacity concept.

evaluations.evidence: must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox
evaluations.rationale: A cancellation-terms checkbox depends on an existing registration/cancellation workflow.

evaluations.evidence: tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists
evaluations.rationale: Explicitly depends on a registration/cancellation workflow being present.

evaluations.evidence: add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site
evaluations.rationale: The story explicitly depends on the existence of a schedule feature.

evaluations.evidence: see which trainings I have signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Requires a training signup/registration capability to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: view ... attached to their training node that shows all attendee information
evaluations.rationale: Depends on training nodes existing and attendees being registered for trainings.

evaluations.evidence: admin view where all trainee information is shown and can be filtered to show a single training session
evaluations.rationale: Depends on trainee data and training sessions existing (i.e., registration/training entities).

evaluations.evidence: dedicated page for each class ... link to register for class
evaluations.rationale: A class detail page can be implemented standalone; the 'link to register' can exist even if registration is handled elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: link to full details of the training
evaluations.rationale: This one-page listing explicitly requires a separate full-details page for trainings.

evaluations.evidence: training landing page ... list of all training offerings
evaluations.rationale: A landing page can be delivered as a standalone page aggregating training offerings without requiring another specific story first.

evaluations.evidence: link on the home page to a list of training options
evaluations.rationale: A link to a list of training options depends on that list page existing.

evaluations.evidence: find out where the coding lounge is and what time it is open
evaluations.rationale: Can be implemented as standalone informational content/page.

evaluations.evidence: refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe
evaluations.rationale: Refunding inherently depends on sponsorship payments being taken/processed first.

evaluations.evidence: find a link on the sponsorships page to become a $350 level sponsor
evaluations.rationale: Depends on the sponsorships page and the ability to become/pay as a sponsor at that level.

evaluations.evidence: See a list of attendees associated with this company
evaluations.rationale: Requires attendee accounts and a company/sponsor association to exist.

evaluations.evidence: identify myself as and pay for a $350 company sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Paying for sponsorship depends on having payment processing/charging capability.

evaluations.evidence: create and maintain venues
evaluations.rationale: Venue CRUD can be implemented as a standalone administrative capability.

evaluations.evidence: view venue details
evaluations.rationale: Viewing venue details depends on venues being created/maintained.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of the sessions associated with sponsor attendees
evaluations.rationale: Depends on sessions existing and on sponsor-attendee associations.

evaluations.evidence: See a payment page ... as the third step of the registration process
evaluations.rationale: Explicitly depends on a multi-step registration process and earlier steps existing.

evaluations.evidence: assign sponsors to events, trainings and summits
evaluations.rationale: Requires sponsors and events/trainings/summits to exist before they can be assigned.

evaluations.evidence: see all events, trainings and summits that a sponsor is sponsoring
evaluations.rationale: Depends on sponsors being assigned to events/trainings/summits.

evaluations.evidence: Enter payment information and have my card charged
evaluations.rationale: Card charging for sponsorship can be implemented as a standalone payment capability without requiring another specific story first.

evaluations.evidence: link BADCamp attendees to my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Requires sponsorship pages and attendee accounts to exist to create the linkage.

evaluations.evidence: update my user profile
evaluations.rationale: Updating a profile depends on having a user account/profile created first.

evaluations.evidence: sign up for the BADCamp newsletter
evaluations.rationale: Newsletter signup can be implemented standalone without depending on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: tag my blog posts for consumption by Drupal Planet

evaluations.evidence: create blog posts

evaluations.evidence: read the blog

evaluations.evidence: sponsor a summit

evaluations.evidence: register for a summit

evaluations.evidence: get detailed directions to the summit venue

evaluations.evidence: see what summits I'm signed up for

evaluations.evidence: see a list of attendees signed up for my summit

evaluations.evidence: list basic information about my summit

evaluations.evidence: list sponsors for my summit

evaluations.evidence: list an agenda for my summit

evaluations.evidence: see how many seats are left for the summit

evaluations.evidence: see specific details on summits

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits

evaluations.evidence: learn about sponsorship levels

evaluations.evidence: use a WYSIWYG editor for all long-form content

evaluations.evidence: learn about posting jobs as a sponsor and contact the sponsorship person

evaluations.evidence: post a job

evaluations.evidence: view the job board
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a job board depends on jobs existing to display.

evaluations.evidence: assign a room to a time slot and a location

evaluations.evidence: see the schedule
